name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (architect → explore → design) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (spec-review-driver.js stepped, the design-driver pattern: deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.23.0 — the 2026-08-21..23 upwell silent-drop incident closed in three parts. (1) `lib/spec-sections.js`'s bare-only trailing-tag rule (rv_640c582f4902) refused a BACKTICKED trailing tag silently, so a host writing genuine `[oracle:]`/`[env:]`/`[pre-green:]` declarations backticked at the trailing position saw them misreported as plain `uncovered-ac`/`unsanctioned-skip`/`unsanctioned-green` with no trace of the cause (upwell: 17 dropped declarations). `parseAcBullets` now also returns `trailingRejected` — the backtick-tolerant trailing run's text when the bare-only run refused it, built from the SAME `TAG_ITEM_SRC` the declaration slot uses, never a second regex authority — and `ac-matrix.js` and `red-check.js` emit the new hard finding `rejected-trailing-tag` in its place, naming the AC-ID, the refused tag, and both readings' remedies. Loud-when-it-bites, never unconditional: the new class REPLACES the generic finding (never both for one AC) only when the refusal is causally relevant, so the illustration bullets the bare-only ban exists to ignore stay silent, and nothing about what PARSES changes. The two manifest leg exits partition by emission site rather than by finding class — a class both loops emit would otherwise redden a leg that observed nothing, a silent misreport into the evidence manifest `verdict.js` reads. (2) New `spec/scripts/lib/frontmatter.js` is the one shared frontmatter-value reader: `spec-review-driver.js` and `spec-design-driver.js` each carried an identical local `fmVal` whose regex captured everything after `key:` including an inline `#` comment — cosmetic on `tier:` until seven live review ledger rows carried a whole sentence inside it, and outright fatal on `build_base:` (rv_e83659d49386). Quoted values return content to the matching close quote; unquoted values strip a whitespace-preceded `#`, so an unspaced `#` inside a URL fragment survives. `spec-status.js` is deliberately untouched — its reader was already correct and it is a frozen critical-tier API. (3) The seven polluted ledger `tier` fields are repaired in place and specs/20260821/03 D8's slipped post-land archaeology is executed as escape rows. 7.22.0 — init-gen.js's four waived defect sites from review rv_e83659d49386 closing — an optional-array shape check for `settings.extraAllow`/`settings.extraDeny` (a string spread per character into the host's permission allow list at exit 0, the one class no error boundary can see), plain-object guards ahead of the two `in`-operator sites on `config.agentMap` and `rules.sections` (a primitive there died as a bare TypeError at Node's implicit exit 1, colliding with the documented manifest-check-red code 1), the settings merge computation moved inside the exit-4 boundary as its first statement (still ahead of every write, so round 2's no-settings-throw-after-a-write ordering holds), and an EISDIR arm on the unreadable-settings refusal so a directory-shaped settings.json is named as a directory instead of being told to chmod a file. The exit-code alphabet is unchanged — exit 2 and exit 4 gain populations, never new meanings. 7.21.0 — `/spec:release`'s ~10-step prose checklist becomes a script, the same move `review-legs.js` made for review: `spec/scripts/release-legs.js` (`spec-paths release-legs`) owns every deterministic release leg through one `stage` subcommand — `substrate` (wraps `manifest-check.sh`), `deploy`, `ready` (a plain retried curl against the deployed `stagingUrl`+`healthPath`; `runtime.readyCheck`'s local-boot contract is the wrong host for a deployed URL, so release.md's old "readyCheck pattern applied to stagingUrl" phrasing — unimplementable as written — is retired, not reused), `migrations` (only when declared runnable), `e2e` (a widened typed-unavailability grammar so `passed`/`failed` admit the same `{"unavailable":…}` shape `skipped` already had — no assumed count without a declared format), and `ci` (the review-legs mapping plus the poll loop release.md used to prescribe in prose, now exactly one row appended per run, never per poll iteration) — plus `append` for the two session-observed legs (`journeys`, `production`) and `record` as the single `verdict.js --profile release --ledger` invocation point on every path alike, STOP and normal close, deriving `--require migrations` itself instead of three separate prose restatements. `release.md` shrinks to judgment steps only — grounding interview, manifest maintenance, journey walks, promote confirm, tag, report — citing the script's own header comment for every row grammar and the poll cadence rather than restating them, the fragile spot that had drifted. The feedback-brief flush retires everywhere it lived (`release.md` Phase 4, `doctor.md` check 12's offer clause, `spec/templates/feedback-brief.md` itself, and the `spec-paths feedback-template` key): its `/intake` consumer died in v7, core § Incident Policy bans intake queues, and § Feedback Loop's carrier list never named briefs — host→plugin signal rides run ledgers and `[plugin]`-tagged Gotchas only. (7.20.0 was the plan-time version target; a concurrent session had already taken it by build time, so this bump lands on the next free minor per the recorded semver-race gotcha.)
